title: Месть поваров за Шефа  (The Cooks' Revenge for the Chef)

segments.t: At the restaurant, Kristina confronts the staff over the mess in the kitchen while Valdemar Barani waves a smug goodbye until tomorrow. Sympathizing with their humiliated boss, Senya and Fedya suggest scratching Barani's car in the courtyard, while Barinov vows to settle the score himself.
Или хотя бы машина ему покоца.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
'I lost track of you.' Kristina answers warmly during the talk, before Barinov can change the subject.

'Forgive me, Kristina.' Barinov lightly chooses this formal apology while facing Kristina using "prostite" ("forgive me") — a warmer, more earnest polite apology that literally asks someone to forgive you.
'Are you aware of this?' Returning to the course beside Kristina, Barinov links the Russian words directly in the present with no word for "am", "is", or "are" needed.
'What your old friend just pulled off?' Kristina presses calmly if there is more going on behind the scenes.
'Just look at that.' Turning frankly during the talk, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'Gentlemen, it was a pleasure meeting you.' Focusing on the gentlemen on the spot, the "-sya" ending on "poznakomitsya" ("to meet") marks an action that unfolds mutually or turns back on the speaker.
'See you tomorrow.' Barinov replies earnestly with a nod, grounding the moment in plain reality.
'Chef, maybe we should kill him, huh?' Kristina fires back candidly in the exchange and lands on "ubit" ("kill") as the key everyday word here.
Или хотя бы машина ему покоца.
'Or at least scratch up his car.' Touching on the car in front of Kristina, Barinov puts the emphasis on "mashina" ("a car") in the middle of the talk.
'You know, that sheep's car.' Kristina opens up firmly beside Barinov, bringing things back to earth after the buildup.
'Leave Volodka alone.' Bringing up the peace in this beat, Barinov reaches for the Russian word "pokoye" ("peace", built from "pokoy") right at the center of the line.
'It broke the man.' Checking on the man with Barinov, spoken Russian compresses the whole thought into just 2 words, skipping the extra helper words English needs.
'We will see who beats whom.' Barinov fires back sharply during the talk, watching Kristina's face to see how the news lands.
Или хотя бы машина ему покоца.

That wraps up this scene as kristina scolds the staff for the damaged equipment, and after Barani leaves for the night, Senya and Fedya offer to vandalize his luxury car to avenge Chef Barinov. Until next time!
